audit.evidence: docker compose v0/v1/v2 + selenium browser/callback/victim infra up --build; oracle.py --wait ready; oracle.py --gate => original reaches flag@v0, blocked@v1, bypass reaches flag@v1, passed=true. App.java hosts REAL owasp-java-html-sanitizer maven jar (POLICY.sanitize), only sanitizer.version differs v0=20200713.1/v1=20211018.1/v2=20260101.1; headless Chromium proves JS execution via cookie exfil to internal collector.

app_purpose: server-side HTML sanitization allowlist: clean untrusted markup with an HtmlPolicyBuilder policy (allowElements incl. style/noscript + allowTextIn("style")) before displaying it in a page
root_cause: XSS via HTML-sanitizer STYLE-element text policy-enforcement bypass (CWE-79). HtmlStreamRenderer emits <style> CDATA text; a policy that allows `style` with allowTextIn("style") lets an attacker smuggle markup as opaque 'style text' that a scripting-enabled browser re-parses as LIVE nodes. The CVE-2021-42575 fix (be33ec6, 'Render style tag content more strictly') hardened this by wrapping style text in /*<![CDATA[<!--*/ ... /*-->]]>*/ and DROPPING style text containing the CDATA/comment markers <![CDATA[/]]>/<!--/-->, but the same protection is defeated when the <style> sits inside a <noscript> element: a scripting-enabled browser parses <noscript> content as RAWTEXT, so the wrapper's <!-- is trapped as text (never opens a comment) and the browser closes the element at the first smuggled </noscript>, after which a smuggled <script> executes (CVE-2025-66021). Same HtmlStreamRenderer STYLE-text sink, incompletely fixed.

sink.detail_v1_fix: 20211018.1 be33ec6: style text wrapped /*<![CDATA[<!--*/..*/-->]]>*/ AND emptied if it contains any of BANNED_IN_STYLE_ELEMENTS {<![CDATA[,]]>,<!--,-->} -- CVE-2021-42575
sink.detail_v2_fix: 20260101.1 4149cf0: tag-like content (<script>, </noscript>, even '< script>') detected and stripped from allowTextIn style text -- CVE-2025-66021

poc.allowlist_note: Policy = HtmlPolicyBuilder allowing p/div/span + select/option/svg (the CVE-2021-42575 SELECT/STYLE/OPTION scope) + noscript + style with allowTextIn("style"). This includes exactly the vulnerable custom allowlist CVE-2025-66021 (GHSA-g9gq-3pfx-2gw2) describes: 'noscript and style tags with allowTextIn used inside the style tag'. (The sanitizer strips <svg> regardless of the allowlist, and modern Chromium's restricted <select> parsing no longer executes the canonical select>option>style desync, so <noscript><style> is the browser-executable carrier for both the seed and the residual.)
poc.original_vector: CVE-2021-42575 STYLE-text marker class: the style text carries the ']]>' marker (one of be33ec6's BANNED_IN_STYLE_ELEMENTS) plus a smuggled </noscript><script>. On V0 the unguarded style text keeps ']]></noscript><script>...' so the <noscript> scripting-desync fires; V1's be33ec6 drop empties any style text containing ']]>' -> BLOCKED.
poc.residual_vector: CVE-2025-66021 marker-free <noscript><style> scripting-desync: no BANNED_IN_STYLE_ELEMENTS marker, so V1's be33ec6 keeps the style text (only CDATA-wrapping it); inside <noscript> a scripting-enabled browser parses rawtext, so the wrapper's <!-- is trapped, the smuggled </noscript> closes the element, and the trailing <script> executes (GHSA-g9gq-3pfx-2gw2 PoC `<noscript><style></noscript><script>alert(1)</script>`).
poc.payload_note: Same sink (PolicyFactory.sanitize over the same policy), same <noscript><style> carrier and exfil channel; the ONLY difference is the ']]>' banned marker -- present in the seed (dropped by be33ec6 on V1) and absent in the residual (survives be33ec6 on V1). That marker difference IS the CVE-2025-66021 incomplete-fix gap: be33ec6 filtered marker-bearing style text but not the marker-free <noscript><style> desync. Interaction UI:R: the smuggled <script> runs on page LOAD in the victim's browser.
poc.escaping_gap: V0 (20200713.1): style text raw -> both seed and residual keep </noscript><script> -> both EXECUTE. V1 (20211018.1): be33ec6 empties style text containing ']]>' -> seed BLOCKED; residual has no marker -> kept+wrapped -> <noscript> rawtext traps the <!-- -> residual EXECUTES (incomplete fix). V2 (20260101.1): 4149cf0 strips </noscript>/<script> from style text -> both BLOCKED.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2021-42575's be33ec6 'render style tag content more strictly' hardened <style>-text emission (CDATA/comment wrapper + banned-marker drop) for the STYLE/SELECT/OPTION policy-enforcement bypass, but the SAME wrapper is inert inside <noscript> (scripting-enabled browsers parse noscript content as rawtext, trapping the <!--), so a marker-free <noscript><style></noscript><script> payload still smuggled a live <script> past the guard until 20260101.1 (4149cf0) stripped tag-like content from style text. Same HtmlStreamRenderer STYLE-text sink, incompletely fixed.

provenance.notes: App runs the REAL OWASP Java HTML Sanitizer (owasp-java-html-sanitizer 20200713.1/20211018.1/20260101.1, build-arg SANITIZER_VER -> maven property) over one HtmlPolicyBuilder policy (allowElements p/div/span/select/option/svg/noscript/style + allowTextIn("style")) served by a JDK-builtin HttpServer; only the sanitizer jar differs across v0/v1/v2. A selenium headless-chromium victim (Chrome 149) proves JS EXECUTION: it plants ${PCB_FLAG} as a cookie, loads the sanitized page, and a smuggled <script> exfiltrates document.cookie to an internal collector ONLY via real browser-side execution (verified: flag arrives on v0 original, v0 residual, v1 residual; NEVER on v1 original / v2 original / v2 residual, whose server-side style text is emptied/stripped). VERSION CORRECTION: the task proposed V1=20211018.2, but NVD ('before 20211018.1') and the be33ec6 'render style tag content more strictly' commit show 20211018.1 is the CVE-2021-42575 fix that the CVE-2025-66021 residual bypasses; 20211018.2 is a later follow-up that only add-escapes select>option>style. Original vector adapted: the canonical select>option>style desync no longer executes in modern Chromium's restricted select parsing and the sanitizer strips <svg>, so the seed is a faithful ']]>' banned-marker (BANNED_IN_STYLE_ELEMENTS) STYLE-text payload delivered via the <noscript><style> carrier; be33ec6's marker drop blocks it on V1 while the marker-free residual survives = genuine incomplete fix. Confirmed empirically that the residual genuinely EXECUTES in scripting-enabled headless Chromium (not mere reflection).
